title: Adjunction morphism is compatible with base change
statement: Let k be a separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], let X be a smooth projective curve over k with a k-rational point σ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] [def-pc-rational-point], and assume that for every k-scheme T the module category on X_T has injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let T and T' be k-schemes, let i : T' ⟶ T be a morphism, and let ℒ ∈ F(T) be an object of the Picard subfunctor [def-pc-f-subfunctor]. Thus its derived direct image is isomorphic to an invertible module placed in degree zero, in the sense of [def-pc-invertible-in-degree-zero]. Write i' : X_{T'} ⟶ X_T for the base change of i [def-pc-base-change]. Then the pullback along i' of the adjunction morphism f_T^* f_{T,*} ℒ ⟶ ℒ is isomorphic, as an arrow, to the adjunction morphism f_{T'}^* f_{T',*}(i'^*ℒ) ⟶ i'^*ℒ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-arrow-iso-pullback-counit] to the same curve, rational point, family of module categories with injective resolutions, morphism i, and Picard-subfunctor object. Its field and geometrically integral hypotheses hold because k is a separably closed field and [prop-pc-xk-integral] states that a smooth projective curve over such a field is geometrically integral. The induced base-change map and pulled-back Picard object are the maps denoted i' and i'^*ℒ here, so the resulting Arrow isomorphism is exactly the asserted compatibility.
